claims.text: stop for a concerning reaction; persistent symptoms need assessment (blocks: key points, 'stop for a concerning reaction', 'use one clear plan')
claims.quote: If you develop an irritated scalp while using this shampoo, stop using it and tell your dermatologist. ... Also, let your dermatologist know if you don't see any improvement in 4 weeks.

claims.text: curly or coily hair: dandruff shampoo about once weekly; general advice does not override a prescription course

claims.text: if you have curly or tightly coiled hair, a dermatologist may recommend dandruff shampoo once a week
claims.quote: However, if you have curly or tightly coiled hair, your dermatologist may recommend using the shampoo once a week.

claims.text: severe or treatment-resistant SD: dermatologist may prescribe oral itraconazole or terbinafine
claims.quote: If this treatment fails to work or you have widespread seborrheic dermatitis, your treatment plan may include: ... Your dermatologist may prescribe an antifungal medication, such as itraconazole or terbinafine.

claims.text: AAD: many patients continue a dandruff shampoo once weekly to prevent flares; maintenance plan after a flare settles
claims.quote: To prevent flare-ups, patients often continue to use dandruff shampoo once a week.

claims.text: this supplement concerns adults; infant cradle cap needs separate age-appropriate advice, not an adult medicated-shampoo regimen

claims.text: scalp psoriasis and other conditions can resemble SD; examination may be needed; a dermatologist can confirm, sometimes with a skin biopsy; the two can occur together (sebopsoriasis)
claims.quote: For example, it's possible to have both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis, which is often called sebopsoriasis. ... If your dermatologist sees signs of two skin conditions, they may remove a small amount of skin. This procedure is called a skin biopsy.

claims.text: examination may be needed; video visit cannot replace every scalp examination
claims.quote: To diagnose this condition, your dermatologist will: ... Look closely at the skin with signs of seborrheic dermatitis.

claims.text: facial SD affects nose, eyebrows, eyelids, ears; may be combined with a mild topical corticosteroid
claims.quote: It can be applied to any skin with seborrheic dermatitis, including the nose, eyebrows, ears, eyelids, and scalp. ... your dermatologist may add a corticosteroid to your treatment plan.

claims.text: when to see a physician: no improvement with OTC care; severe or treatment-resistant cases (red or raw skin, spread, hair loss, daily-life impact not stated on this page)
claims.quote: If this treatment fails to work or you have widespread seborrheic dermatitis ... Also, let your dermatologist know if you don't see any improvement in 4 weeks.

claims.text: hair shedding or patchy loss should not automatically be blamed on dandruff; other scalp conditions can look similar

claims.text: thought to result from an inflammatory response to Malassezia yeast

claims.text: AFP review advises beginning scalp treatment with an OTC shampoo

claims.text: OTC options (zinc pyrithione, selenium sulfide) reasonable for mild scalp SD/dandruff

claims.text: corticosteroids are a short-term bridge, not long-term
claims.quote: Antifungal shampoos (long-term) and topical corticosteroids (short-term) can be used as second-line agents for treatment of scalp seborrheic dermatitis.

claims.text: low- or mid-potency corticosteroids reduce symptoms
claims.quote: Low- or mid-potency topical corticosteroids have been successful in reducing symptoms of seborrheic dermatitis

claims.text: long-term steroid use associated with skin thinning and telangiectasia
claims.quote: long-term use has been associated with thinning of the skin and formation of telangiectasia

claims.text: calcineurin inhibitors: FDA boxed warning; evidence insufficient; avoid continuous long-term use

claims.text: can also appear on chest, back, axillae, groin

claims.text: zinc scalp treatment at six and 11 months showed no loss of effect
claims.quote: a study evaluating a zinc scalp treatment at six and 11 months showed no loss of effect.

claims.text: FDA approved for SD in adults and children 9 and older

claims.quote: Apply a thin layer of ZORYVE foam, 0.3%, once daily to affected areas of body and/or scalp when they are not wet.

claims.text: facial SD is common; affects sides of the nose, eyebrows, eyelids, forehead
claims.quote: nasolabial folds, upper eyebrows, and the nasal bridge ... Note erythema of the eyelid, nasolabial fold, and forehead.

claims.text: facial SD produces redness, oiliness and fine flaking
claims.quote: Clinically, seborrheic dermatitis presents as symmetric, poorly defined erythematous patches with yellow, oily scales and fine, superficial desquamation (flaking).

claims.text: SD common and chronic relapsing; face treated with antifungal and corticosteroid creams
claims.quote: Seborrheic dermatitis is a common, chronic relapsing skin condition ... Seborrheic dermatitis of the face and body can be treated with over-the-counter and prescription-strength antifungal creams, over-the-counter and prescription-strength corticosteroid creams

references.notes: New on main. Page does not discuss hair loss and does not say what each ingredient does; it lists ingredients to look for.

claims.text: read the active ingredient and follow your own bottle; ingredient-based options (zinc pyrithione, selenium sulfide, ketoconazole, salicylic acid, coal tar)
claims.quote: Zinc pyrithione; salicylic acid; sulfur; selenium sulfide; ketoconazole; and coal tar shampoo ... Follow the instructions on the dandruff shampoo bottle.

claims.text: AAD suggests alternating or trying a different active ingredient if one does not help
claims.quote: If one shampoo doesn't work, try alternating between dandruff shampoos with different active ingredients.

claims.text: curly/coily hair: apply to scalp, attention to dryness, about once weekly; normal shampoo and conditioner can follow
claims.quote: use your dandruff shampoo about once a week, if tolerated. ... Take care to only apply the dandruff shampoo to your scalp if you have curly or coily hair ... as the ingredients that treat dandruff can dry your hair. ... You can shampoo and condition your hair with your normal products ... after using your dandruff shampoo if it is needed for hair care.

claims.text: AAD notes some products need several minutes, but directions vary
claims.quote: You may also need to allow some dandruff shampoos to sit on your scalp for up to 5-10 minutes before rinsing.

claims.text: persistent dandruff deserves a diagnosis check; psoriasis, fungal infection and other conditions can resemble it; refractory disease may need dermatology care
claims.quote: If your dandruff doesn't go away after following these tips ... partner with a board-certified dermatologist ... knows whether your dandruff is a sign of a medical condition ... such as seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis, fungal infections of the scalp, or eczema.

claims.text: mild symptoms may be approached with label-directed OTC care
claims.quote: For most people, dandruff does not require medical attention.

claims.text: other dandruff shampoos can contain different active ingredients such as zinc pyrithione or salicylic acid (sentence corrected this run)
claims.quote: Zinc pyrithione; salicylic acid; sulfur; selenium sulfide; ketoconazole; and coal tar shampoo

claims.text: patchy hair loss needs assessment (page does not mention hair loss)
claims.quote: If your dandruff doesn't go away after following these tips ... partner with a board-certified dermatologist

references.notes: Prescription label (Actavis Pharma; manufactured for Teva). Printed date corrected this run from 'Label revised November 2024' to 'Label revised October 2023'; no November 2024 date appears on the page. Indicated for scalp SD in adults.

claims.text: ciclopirox 1% label specifies 3 minutes on the scalp, then rinse
claims.quote: Lather and leave on hair and scalp for 3 minutes. ... A timer may be used. ... Avoid contact with eyes. Rinse off.

claims.text: twice weekly for 4 weeks, at least 3 days apart (citable summary)
claims.quote: Treatment should be repeated twice per week for 4 weeks, with a minimum of 3 days between applications.

claims.text: review diagnosis if no improvement after 4 weeks
claims.quote: If a patient with seborrheic dermatitis shows no clinical improvement after 4 weeks of treatment ... the diagnosis should be reviewed.

claims.text: stop for a concerning reaction; tell the prescriber about irritation
claims.quote: If a reaction suggesting sensitivity or irritation occurs with the use of Ciclopirox Shampoo 1%, ... treatment should be discontinued and appropriate therapy instituted.

claims.text: avoid the eyes
claims.quote: Contact of Ciclopirox Shampoo 1% with the eyes should be avoided.

claims.text: label reports hair adverse effects incl. hair loss; spontaneous reports cannot establish frequency or causation
claims.quote: hair discoloration and abnormal hair texture, alopecia, irritation and rash ... Because these events are reported voluntarily from a population of uncertain size, ... it is not possible to reliably estimate their frequency or establish a causal relationship to drug exposure.

claims.text: if the prescribed schedule irritates, ask the prescriber to adjust
claims.quote: Inform the physician if the area of application shows signs of increased irritation
